command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'
/bin/bash -c "python3 -c \"import importlib.util; print({m: bool(importlib.util.find_spec(m)) for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']})\""

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text=p.extract_text()
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{text}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt tmp/pdfs/page-15.txt tmp/pdfs/page-16.txt tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt'
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-23.txt tmp/pdfs/page-24.txt tmp/pdfs/page-25.txt tmp/pdfs/page-26.txt tmp/pdfs/page-27.txt tmp/pdfs/page-28.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from fractions import Fraction as F
# Lemma 4: symmetric, irreducible, aperiodic two-state MRP, one normalized feature.
p=F(1,10)
gamma=F(9,10)
transition_feature_eigenvalue=2*p-1
A=gamma*transition_feature_eigenvalue-1
print('Lemma 4 example: P=[[0.1,0.9],[0.9,0.1]], pi=(0.5,0.5), Phi=(1,-1)"'^T, gamma=0.9'"')
print('Sigma=1; A=',float(A),'; A"'^T A='"',float(A*A),'; Lipschitz factor=',float(abs(A)))
# Eq. (4), unscaled sign, positive scalar input.
x=F(1,10)
print('Unscaled sign at x=0.1: squared compression error=',float((1-x)**2),'; squared input norm=',float(x*x))
# Theorem 4, deterministic map with finite one-state aperiodic chain, identity compression.
alpha=F(1,2)
beta=1
multipliers=(1-alpha,1-10*alpha)
print('Theorem 4 example: g(theta)=-diag(1,10)theta, L=10, beta=1, delta=1, alpha=0.5')
print('alpha*beta=',float(alpha*beta),'; update multipliers=',tuple(map(float,multipliers)))
print('From theta_0=(0,1), squared error at t=5:',float(multipliers[1]**10))
PY"

strengths: Originality: Extending established error-feedback techniques to TD directions and Markovian stochastic approximation offers useful new understanding. The joint analysis of memory, projection, and temporal dependence is more substantive than simply applying an existing compressor.

Significance: Communication-efficient policy evaluation is a worthwhile problem. Theorem 5 separates a compression-independent leading variance term proportional to 1/(MT) from compression-dependent higher-order terms, providing a useful characterization under independent stationary sampling.

Soundness strengths: The perturbed-iterate identities and coupled Lyapunov approach provide a coherent analytical framework. Extensive appendices expose the intermediate recursions and make the arguments assessable.

Presentation: The progression from deterministic dynamics through stochastic and distributed settings is easy to follow. Explicit algorithms, proof sketches, and comparisons with uncompressed TD help explain the contribution.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript candidly acknowledges the projection requirement, the unresolved compression tradeoff under Markovian sampling, and the absence of a stability proof for unprojected experiments. The synthetic experiments raise no apparent material research-ethics concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—Theorem 4 does not establish its stated guarantee for Algorithm 1. Appendix F relies on projection and bounded iterates inherited from Eq. (38), whereas Algorithm 1 has no projection. Its stated condition αβ < 1 permits divergence: with identity compression and deterministic g(θ) = −diag(1,10)θ, Assumptions 1–3 hold with L=10 and β=1, but α=0.5 multiplies the second coordinate by −4 each iteration. The theorem must explicitly specify the projected algorithm and required bounds, or supply sufficient stability conditions for the unprojected algorithm.

Soundness—the advertised sign compressor is outside the assumed class as described. Section 3 says each coordinate is replaced by its sign and claims this satisfies Eq. (4). For scalar x=0.1, the squared compression error is 0.81, while Eq. (4)'s right-hand side is at most 0.01. A suitably norm-scaled sign compressor can satisfy the assumption, but its definition and implementation are missing. Consequently, the guarantees do not substantiate the stated SignTD instantiation or its experimental implementation.

Proof correctness—Lemma 4 incorrectly claims that the mean TD direction is 1-Lipschitz and that AᵀA ≼ Σ. Consider P=[[0.1,0.9],[0.9,0.1]], γ=0.9, and the normalized feature column Φ=(1,−1)ᵀ. Then Σ=1 and A=−1.72, contradicting both claims. A bound of 2 is available, so this appears repairable through constant changes, but downstream arguments need correction. Lemma 6 also sets η=δ−1 while asserting a contraction factor obtained with η=2(δ−1).

Communication claims exceed the analyzed model. The top-1 argument counts a nonzero coordinate as approximately constant bits without specifying the precision needed to encode its real-valued magnitude. Algorithm 2 additionally broadcasts the full K-dimensional model every round. The claimed bit budget needs an explicit encoding model and a clear restriction to uplink communication.

The practical reach of the linear-speedup claim needs qualification. Theorem 5 assumes independent samples across time and agents from the same stationary distribution. Moreover, comparing its two stochastic terms shows that compression becomes lower order only when T is roughly larger than δ²M/[ω(1−γ)²], ignoring logarithms. With top-1 compression, δ=K, so this transient can be substantial. The statement that communication efficiency comes almost for free understates this dependence.

Reproducibility and evaluation are inadequate. Section 8 omits experimental step sizes, initializations, precise transition-matrix and feature-generation procedures, random seeds, and a code link. Although 30 trials are reported, uncertainty intervals are absent. Figures 4–5 illustrate reduced parameter-error floors, whereas Theorem 5 concerns a weighted average and value-function error; these plots therefore provide limited direct validation of the claimed convergence rate. The missing sign-compressor specification further obstructs reproduction.
